subject: Question about specifying simple binomial hierarchical model

messages.author: 497eb9c410b69640
messages.subject: Question about specifying simple binomial hierarchical model
parts:
This is a really basic question, but I haven't worked with the formula notation used by brms earlier, so I'm a bit confused.

Suppose I have run an a/b-test in 10 different countries, where the outcome is that either a user did convert or it didn't. I.e. I wan't to fit a model like this

Conversions ~ Binomial(n_users, p)
p = inv_logit(a + a_country + (b + b_country)*condition)

Where:
a is the overall intercept
a_country is the deflection from that intercept for each country
b is the overall slope
b_country is the deflection from the overall slope for each country
condition is a dummy variable, 1 if the user was in the test group and 0 if it was in the control group.

a_country and b_country should be hierarchical terms that are drawn from some over-arching distribution (ideally correlated)

How does one fit such a model with brms?

This is the model I have arrived at so far:

model <- brm(
  formula = conversions | trials(users) ~ (condition | country),
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = data
)

The output from that model looks correct, but I can't quite work out how I can get samples for the b parameter (the overall slope) in an efficient way....
